fix.notes: The local import pattern (`from decksite.data import person as person_data` inside `add_deck`) is the standard approach to break circular imports in this codebase. No behaviour change — the function body is identical; only the module it lives in changes.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`get_or_insert_person_id` existed as an identical duplicate in both `decksite/data/deck.py` (lines 453-459) and `decksite/data/person.py` (lines 272-278). The canonical home for this function is `person.py` since it inserts/selects from the `person` table. However:
- `deck.add_deck()` was calling the local copy on `deck.py`
- `person.link_discord()` was calling `deck.get_or_insert_person_id()` (the wrong module)

The duplicate on `deck.py` existed to avoid a circular import (`person.py` imports `deck` at module level, so `deck.py` cannot import `person` at module level).

## What changed

- **`decksite/data/deck.py`**: Deleted the duplicate `get_or_insert_person_id` function (8 lines). In `add_deck()`, added a local (function-scoped) import `from decksite.data import person as person_data` and changed the call to `person_data.get_or_insert_person_id(...)`. The local import avoids the circular-import issue.
- **`decksite/data/person.py`**: Changed `person.link_discord()` to call the local `get_or_insert_person_id(...)` directly instead of `deck.get_or_insert_person_id(...)`.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped, 89 deselected

Fixes #11997
